channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Labor market soft, RBNZ hike eyed – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Australia/NZ macro team sees New Zealand Employment growth at 0.1% q/q in Q2, insufficient to match population gains. They expect the Unemployment Rate to rise to 5.4%, returning to its recent cycle high and aligning with the RBNZ’s May forecast.

item.title: US Dollar: FOMC fallout weighs on USD – MUFG
item.description: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the US Dollar index has fallen back below 100.00 following last week’s FOMC meeting, as the Fed left rates on hold and Chair Kevin Warsh offered less hawkish guidance.

item.title: Silver shines near $60 as falling Oil supports precious metals
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) trades around $59.80 at the time of writing on Tuesday, up 2.81% on the day.

item.title: Copper: Tariff uncertainty and tight supply – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes Copper is surging as tighter availability meets uncertainty over United States (US) tariffs, with shipments to the United States draining inventories elsewhere and constrained mine output leaving the market exposed to squeezes.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Joint intervention lifts JPY against US Dollar – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley highlights that Japanese authorities benefited from the post-FOMC US Dollar (USD) drop, which eased pressure on the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: GBP/JPY Price Forecast: Bears test 200-day SMA after sharp sell-off
item.description: GBP/JPY rises on Tuesday as the Japanese Yen (JPY) gives back part of its recent rally, which was driven by coordinated intervention from Tokyo and Washington.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says Hormuz deal nears as Oil prices tumble
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a CNBC interview on Tuesday that a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz could be reached as soon as Tuesday or Wednesday. He added that he expects energy prices to "settle back down".

item.title: Natural gas: Tight market but less stressed – ING
item.description: ING’s commodities team points out that European gas prices fell, with TTF down modestly, as the market digests storage and demand trends.

item.title: US Dollar: JOLTS openings seen retreating – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect US JOLTS job openings to fall to 7.0 million in June from 7.594 million in May, below the 7.504 million consensus forecast, as the recent increase appears difficult to sustain. They expect the data to move closer to softer private-sector hiring indicators.

item.title: Euro defends the 1.1500 level ahead of a string of US labour data
item.description: The Euro (EUR) posts marginal gains against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday as Monday’s reversal from three-week highs at 1.1560 has been contained at 1.1500 so far.

item.title: Oil: Supply resilience and geopolitical risks – BNY
item.description: BNY's Geoff Yu reports that Saudi Aramco sees no material operational or financial impact from July attacks, with alternative pipelines, storage and export terminals preserving output.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Relief rallies seen as selling opportunity – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/JPY has fully retraced its prior slump and is testing key resistance at the 200-day moving average near 158.02.

item.title: Qatar’s Ansari: Efforts are ongoing to seek diplomatic solution in US-Iran conflict
item.description: Qatar's Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Majed Al Ansari, confirms during the European trading session on Tuesday that efforts are ongoing with the United States (US) and Iran to seek a diplomatic resolution. Ansari added, “What is important right now is getting back to the negotiation talks.”

item.title: Gold: Rebound supported by lower energy – ING
item.description: ING strategist Ewa Manthey highlights that Gold has extended its recovery, posting its first monthly gain since February. The metal is supported by easing Middle East geopolitical tensions and sharply lower Oil prices, which reduce inflation concerns.

item.title: Gold holds steady as traders weigh US-Iran talks, Fed outlook
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades flat on Tuesday, extending its sideways grind as uncertainty surrounding US-Iran peace efforts and the Federal Reserve’s (Fed) monetary policy path keeps traders cautious.

item.title: British Pound finds footing at 1.3420 with markets awaiting US Job Openings data
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) edges higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, reaching session highs above 1.3440 after finding support at the 1.3420 area earlier on the day.

item.title: Indian Rupee struggles for direction as RBI policy awaited
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades flat at around 95.33 against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday. The Indian currency is expected to trade sideways as investors await the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) monetary policy announcement on Wednesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade surplus seen narrowing – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect Canada’s International Merchandise Trade surplus to narrow in June as weaker Oil prices weigh on energy exports. They forecast a surplus of $2.5bn versus the market’s $3.0bn and May’s $4.2bn.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD remains sideways around $4,050 during US NFP week
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) remains in a tight range at around $4,050 during the European trading session on Tuesday. The precious metal struggles to get direction, with investors awaiting the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for July, which will be released later this week.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens despite intervention warnings as USD/JPY rebounds near 158
item.description: USD/JPY trades around 157.95 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 0.49% on the day.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Dollar, capped at 0.8100, hints at a potential “H&S” pattern
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) shows marginal losses against the Swiss Franc (CHF) on Tuesday, as Dollar bulls struggle to find acceptance above 0.8100.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Downside bias within defined range – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang notes that the USD Index bias has shifted to the downside after failing to break above the weekly Ichimoku cloud and instead plunging below the 55-week EMA.

item.title: Indian Rupee: RBI pause and Special swap inflows – DBS
item.description: DBS economist Radhika Rao expects the RBI MPC to keep the benchmark rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance and cautious guidance.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Managed JPY signals new order – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Senior Market Strategist Benjamin Picton highlights coordinated action between the US Treasury and Japan’s Ministry of Finance (MoF) to defend the Japanese Yen (JPY), framing it as a potential “financial Fort Sumter” in capital markets.

item.title: Euro advances as ECB tightening expectations, Japan fiscal concerns weigh on Yen
item.description: EUR/JPY trades around 181.70 on Tuesday, up 0.44% on the day at the time of writing, supported by renewed optimism surrounding the Euro (EUR) and persistent weakness in the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Tuesday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.86 per troy ounce, up 1.15% from the $58.19 it cost on Monday.

item.title: South African Rand: Rate hold seen hurting currency – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur writes that despite South Africa’s reasonable recent performance under pressure from the Iran conflict, the central bank’s July decision to leave its key rate unchanged was surprising.

item.title: US Dollar: NFP and inflation mix complicate Fed path – BNY
item.description: BNY strategists John Velis and David Tam highlight the July Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report and upcoming Consumer Price Index (CPI) releases as key inputs for the Fed. They see consensus around 80,000 jobs, with a breakeven near 50,000 to keep unemployment steady.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Jobs data and RBNZ hiking path – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole expects New Zealand’s Q2 labour data to broadly match the Reserve Bank of New Zealand’s May projections, which implied one to two hikes in Q3. He favours a hike in September or October, with rising conviction for September.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Holds steady near 0.5870 as bullish bias remains
item.description: The NZD/USD pair seesaws between tepid gains and minor losses through the first half of the European session on Tuesday, stalling the previous day's retracement slide from a two-month high – levels just above the 0.5900 mark.
